comparisons.peer_summary: Manufacturing depends on third-party manufacturers and foundries, yet many contracts lack long-term capacity or pricing commitments. This exposes the company to risks where suppliers may allocate capacity elsewhere, leading to unavailability of materials at reasonable prices or inability to meet demand spikes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose significant reliance on third-party manufacturing and supply chain limitations in Item 1. Intel specifically highlights its reliance on government incentives and private capital (SCIP) to support its 'accelerated manufacturing build-outs' and domestic capacity. Micron similarly discloses that its 'manufacturing processes are also dependent on our relationships with... outsourced semiconductor foundries' and explicitly warns that 'many of these contracts do not provide for long-term capacity or pricing commitments,' exposing the company to risks of capacity allocation by suppliers. While Intel focuses on the strategic financing and incentive drivers of its manufacturing expansion, Micron details the operational supply chain risks inherent in third-party manufacturing dependencies.

sentences.text: ▪SCIP. We access strategically aligned private capital to increase our flexibility and help efficiently accelerate and scale manufacturing build-outs. Our SCIP program has supported the period of accelerated manufacturing investment that commenced in early 2021. We signed our latest SCIP agreement in the second quarter of 2024 and are not contemplating further transactions in the near term.
▪Government incentives. We work with governments to advance and benefit from incentives for domestic manufacturing capacity for leading-edge semiconductors.

Our manufacturing processes are also dependent on our relationships with third-party manufacturers of controllers, analog integrated circuits, and other components used in some of our products and with outsourced semiconductor foundries, assembly and test providers, contract manufacturers, logistics carriers, and other service providers, including providers of maintenance for our advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment and providers of electricity and other utilities.

To the extent we do not have firm commitments from our third-party suppliers over a specific time period or for any specific capacity, quantity, and/or pricing, our suppliers may allocate capacity to their other customers and capacity and/or materials may not be available when needed or at reasonable prices.

comparisons.peer_topic: Supply chain resilience and inventory management policies
comparisons.peer_summary: To build redundancy and align capacity with growing demand, the company has expanded supplier relationships and may place non-cancellable orders, pay premiums, or provide deposits for components in periods of growth.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both disclose active strategies to secure manufacturing capacity and supply chain resilience in Item 1. Intel describes accessing 'strategically aligned private capital' via SCIP to 'accelerate and scale manufacturing build-outs.' NVIDIA mirrors this proactive supply securing approach by stating it has 'expanded our supplier relationships to build redundancy' and may 'place non-cancellable inventory orders... pay premiums, or provide deposits to secure future supply and capacity.' Both companies are actively managing capital and operational levers to ensure sufficient manufacturing capacity for their growth, though Intel emphasizes capital structures (SCIP/governments) while NVIDIA emphasizes procurement tactics (non-cancellable orders/deposits).

sentences.text: ▪SCIP. We access strategically aligned private capital to increase our flexibility and help efficiently accelerate and scale manufacturing build-outs. Our SCIP program has supported the period of accelerated manufacturing investment that commenced in early 2021. We signed our latest SCIP agreement in the second quarter of 2024 and are not contemplating further transactions in the near term.

In periods of growth, we may place non-cancellable inventory orders for certain product components in advance of our historical lead times, pay premiums, or provide deposits to secure future supply and capacity and may need to continue to do so.
We have expanded our supplier relationships to build redundancy and resilience in our operations to provide long-term manufacturing capacity aligned with growing customer demand.
